Christmas-morning follow-up with ER charge nurse Alyssa Cortez after her Christmas Eve shift; cold-weather heating and carbon monoxide guidance.

Came off her volunteered twelve-hour Christmas Eve shift a little after 7 a.m. Christmas morning; gave her spare granola bar to a teammate around 3 a.m.; 'After this year, regular is a present'; warned against heating with ovens, grills or generators indoors; not working New Year's Eve ('Somebody else gets to find the eye wash'). No patient details.
Christmas Day roundup: Port Aransas bait shop closed, church service near the bay, Elizondo family.

Shop closed Christmas Day (sign: 'CLOSED CHRISTMAS DAY. GO SEE YOUR FAMILY.'); drove by with coffee to look at it; 'In September this was four walls and a smell. Now it's a store'; 'Shop rules, and I wrote them.'
Christmas morning service at her church beside the fellowship hall; 'Yesterday we fed people. Today we sing'; hub reopens after Christmas.

At Whitfield's Christmas service with her three kids; two gifts came from the hub toy table, the third rode home with her on the bus; glad not to explain 'the transfer downtown'; bucket Bob still under the hallway leak; landlord says repairs after the holidays.

Year-end port-conditions reference: X-Ray Sat., Sept. 11 (port open), Yankee Sun., Sept. 12 (inbound closed, 14 inbound vessels at anchorage), Zulu Mon., Sept. 13 (all traffic; anchorage ships put to sea), ships back at the anchorage Fri., Sept. 17.
'Port conditions follow the forecast, not the calendar'; X-Ray is the time to plan, Yankee the time to move; by Zulu every vessel should already be where it rides out the weather.
